what: the occupancy intervention re-run twice on each of two MI355X dies, to separate run-to-run noise from a per-card difference
generator: AI/probe_rmsnorm_occupancy_intervention.py, run 2x on HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 and 2x on 4; this file assembled from the four sidecars
why: I published, and told the team, that this intervention 'reproduces across two GPUs to within 0.2% on every bandwidth figure'. That was devices 6 and 5. Device 4 breaks it: every row is faster there, by 1.7% to 11.0%, reproducibly. Two runs per device separate the two candidate explanations and the answer is not noise -- worst within-device spread 1.08%, worst between-device gap 10.96%.
direction: device 4 is faster on every row, despite a LOWER streaming ceiling than device 5

streaming_ceiling_tbps_two_read_one_writ.note: same probe as the cliff sidecar's ceiling, 512 MiB, min of 10x20. Device 4 is the slowest of the three at pure streaming and the fastest at this kernel, so normalising by a per-device ceiling would WIDEN the gap, not close it. Whatever device 4 is doing better is not raw bandwidth.

what_does_reproduce.registers_and_spills: identical on every row across all four runs -- the compiler output does not depend on which die runs it, as expected, which is why the register story is unaffected
what_does_reproduce.occupancy: within 0.6% on every row; see per-row occupancy_device4/5
what_does_reproduce.reading: the claims this experiment makes are all ratios -- the none->2 lift, the flat control, the equal-occupancy pair -- and those agree across dies to about a percentage point. It is the ABSOLUTE pct_of_ceiling figures that are per-card.

unexplained: why device 4 is faster. Idle sclk/mclk/fclk/socclk are identical across 4/5/6 and junction temperatures are within 2C. Not investigated further: it does not bear on any conclusion here, and saying 'reproduces across GPUs' without checking a third die is what produced the wrong claim in the first place.
bonus: this is a third, unplanned instance of the equal-occupancy argument. Occupancy matches across dies to 0.6% while bandwidth differs by up to 11%, so occupancy again fails to determine bandwidth -- this time with the kernel, the registers and the spills all held exactly fixed.
